hits.text:
A Chinese film studio wired DeepSeek V4 into Blender, and the cheapest model in the room is now doing the work nobody wanted to pay a person for

Hero assets still go to artists. Everything behind them - the volume of a production nobody notices - now gets generated.

> FILL - background props and set dressing generated per shot instead of reused
> SCALE - every asset checked against the scene’s real dimensions before placement
> VARY - repeated objects given natural variation, so crowds stop looking copy-pasted
> LOD - low-detail versions built automatically for anything far from camera
> CLEAN - topology and naming normalised so the pipeline accepts the output untouched

Background work is the quiet majority of a film’s asset budget. It never gets praised, and it always gets cut for time.

So productions reuse. The same crate, the same chair, the same crowd, and audiences feel the repetition without naming it.

Variation is cheap now. Forty slightly different crates cost barely more than forty copies of one.

The LOD pass is the real production saving. Far geometry at full density is pure render time spent on pixels nobody sees.

Cheap tokens change what is worth generating. At DeepSeek’s price the question stops being whether to fill a shot properly.

The shot setup, the variation rules and a full dressed scene are laid out underneath.

This is f*cking gold..

Chinese researchers just published a paper that kills the hottest skill of the year: "The End of Context Engineering".

The argument fits in one line: a context window packed by a human is a guess made before the model has looked.

You pack what you would have needed. The model needs something else. Too much of the obvious, none of the surprising.

So the paper hands the model an index instead: one line per thing that exists, never the content. The model names what it needs, pulls only that, runs the task, and every item gets credited or blamed for the result.

Anthropic turned a model loose on sequencing data nobody could classify and pulled out a virus that matches nothing on record

It was never looking for a virus. The question was what the leftovers are - the reads every pipeline throws away as junk.

> KEEP - the unclassified fraction of each dataset retained instead of discarded
> SHAPE - those reads assembled by structure, with no reference genome to lean on
> HOST - each assembly matched to what else was living in the same sample

Every sequencing run produces a pile that matches nothing. Standard practice is to delete it and move on.

That pile is not noise. It is mostly things with no close relative in any database, which is the definition of undiscovered.

Assembling without a reference is the hard part. You cannot align to something known when nothing known is close.

The host step is what makes it useful. A sequence alone says little; a sequence plus what it was living inside says a lot.

Most of the biosphere has never been catalogued, and the evidence has been sitting in discarded data for years.

The assembly method and what the samples contained are laid out underneath.

→ Before a sales call: what a company has actually been doing
→ To keep up with AI: what the community figured out this week
→ Polymarket odds are included, so you see where real money is betting

Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket and GitHub work with zero setup. A 30-second wizard unlocks X, YouTube and TikTok.

/plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill
/plugin install last30days

CURSOR 🔥:
- Cursor cloud agents can now build interactive canvases like dashboards and reports that can be shared as a link.
